# Callisto's build-matrix release flow for napi platform packages
# (docs/releasing.md in orin-dx/callisto): a push to main either refreshes the
# Callisto version PR or, for a merged version PR, runs plan -> build ->
# execute. Keep this filename: Callisto's recovery docs and coordinator
# identity name `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto version-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto version PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release: ${{ steps.decision.outputs.is_release }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:

      # parent-to-merge delta. A release must also be a GitHub-verified merge
      # of the managed PR, never a direct push.
      - name: Check release-source provenance
        id: provenance
        env:

          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}

# Affected-only lint: uses moon's dependency-graph-aware affected-project
# detection to build the crate scope, then feeds it into ONE cargo
# invocation with multiple -p flags. This is the incremental counterpart to
# `lint` (which lints the whole workspace in one shot) -- it exists so a

# and "fan out one cargo process per crate" (the latter serializes behind
# Cargo's shared target/ lock; see .moon/tasks/rust.yml). Only lints the
# affected crates' own source, not their downstream dependents -- clippy
# warnings are about a crate's own code, not its callers.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id // empty')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No affected crates; skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    # Root-level changes (manifests, toolchain, lint config) affect every crate.
    if grep -qx michi-workspace <<< "$projects"; then
        echo "Workspace root affected; linting every crate."
        cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    while IFS= read -r p; do
        args+=(-p "$p")
    done <<< "$projects"
    echo "Linting affected crates: ${args[*]}"
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

# Architecture

This document describes how the `michi` workspace crates fit together.

## Workspace Layout

`michi` is structured as a virtual Cargo workspace (the root `Cargo.toml` has no `[package]`) with two published crates in `crates/` and one unpublished binding crate in `packages/`:

```text
michi (workspace root, virtual manifest)
├── crates/
│   ├── michi-core        # Every sync primitive: toon, kv, hints, recovery, empty, error, status, mcp, audience,
│   │                     #   response (AgentResponse), pipeline (data type), truncate, truncation, resilience, telemetry;
│   │                     #   napi (feature)
│   ├── michi-graph       # MIT, no dependencies: dependency graphs (GraphBuilder, Graph, Dag), validation, order, layers
│   └── michi-pipeline    # Async pipeline execution: Plan, execute/resume, RunRecord, BreakerRegistry, CancellationToken
└── packages/michi-node   # Node.js NAPI cdylib (@orin-dx/michi), publish = false
```

Dependency direction:

```mermaid
graph LR
    core["michi-core"]
    graphcrate["michi-graph (MIT)"]
    pipeline["michi-pipeline"]
    node["packages/michi-node (@orin-dx/michi)"]

    pipeline --> core
    pipeline --> graphcrate
    node -- "features = [napi]" --> core
```

`michi-core`, `michi-pipeline` and `michi-node` version in lockstep (each crate's `version`, kept equal by Callisto), released together as a Callisto fixed group. `michi-graph` is MIT, depends on nothing in michi and versions on its own; `michi-pipeline` takes it through a normal `^` range and keeps its types out of its public API. `michi-pipeline` and `michi-node` depend on `michi-core` through an exact `=x.y.z` workspace pin, so a mixed set never resolves.

## Component Overview

| Crate / Package | Responsibility | Runtime Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `michi-core` | All sync AXI primitives. `toon`: TOON list rendering and parsing with stack-inlined `CompactString` cells. `truncate`: UTF-8 char-boundary content truncation (`floor_char_boundary`). `truncation`: `TruncationOutcome`, the report of what a list cap cut. `resilience`: retry back-off math, `Retry-After` HTTP date parsing, FNV-1a idempotency keys. Response DTOs: `AgentResponse`, `DomainError`, `StatusResponse`, `CallToolResult`, and the `Pipeline` data type. The public `resilience`, `truncate` and `truncation` items are re-exported at the crate root by explicit list. | `thiserror`, `compact_str` (Optional: `serde`, `serde_json`, `schemars`, `miette`, `napi`, `napi-derive`) |
| `michi-pipeline` | Async execution of a validated `Plan` of steps: one `JoinSet` scheduler (sequential or capped parallel), a returned `RunRecord` whose statuses are `michi-core`'s `StepStatus`, `resume` from a record, a keyed `BreakerRegistry`, a per-run `RetryBudget`, `CancellationToken` and a `StepObserver`. Own `ExecutionError` and `PlanError` types, converting into `DomainError` via `From` — not variants of `michi_core::Error`. See `docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md`. | `michi-core`, `michi-graph`, `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `thiserror` (optional: `serde`) |
| `michi-graph` | MIT, `no_std` + `alloc`. Deterministic dependency graphs: `GraphBuilder` declares nodes and kinded edges, `Graph` may hold cycles, and validation returns a `Dag` or every violation at once. Topological order, layers, ready sets, ancestors and descendants, all following one caller-chosen tie-break. See `docs/spec/09-graph.md`. | none |
| `packages/michi-node` | NAPI cdylib shim for `@orin-dx/michi`. Not published to crates.io. | `michi-core` (`napi` feature), `napi`, `napi-derive` |

## Data Composition & Render Flow

`michi` provides two main entry points for formatting output:

1. **`response::AgentResponse` (Fluent Builder)**: Composes TOON lists, KV items, `help[]` hints, and recovery guidance into a unified output buffer. Supports assistant/user audience routing and direct conversion to MCP `CallToolResult`.
2. **Standalone DTOs**: `DomainError`, `StatusResponse`, `AlreadyDone`, and `empty_state()` render themselves directly into agent-readable KV blocks or GitHub Actions annotations without passing through `AgentResponse`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph primitives["Primitives"]
        toon["michi-core::toon"]
        kv["michi-core::kv"]
        hints["michi-core::hints"]
        recovery["michi-core::recovery"]
        truncate["michi-core::truncate"]
        truncation["michi-core::truncation"]
    end

    toon --> AR
    kv --> AR
    hints --> AR
    recovery --> AR
    truncate --> AR
    truncation --> AR

    AR["michi-core::AgentResponse"]

    AR -->|"render() / render_toon() / render_kv()"| text["Plain Text CLI / Tool Stdout"]
    AR -->|"render_for(Audience)"| textaud["Audience-Routed Output"]
    AR -->|"to_call_tool_result()"| mcpresult["mcp::CallToolResult"]
    mcpresult --> mcpjson["MCP Tools/Call JSON"]

    subgraph standalone["Standalone Renderers"]
        err["DomainError"]
        status["StatusResponse"]
        empty["empty_state()"]
    end

    err --> text
    status --> text
    empty --> text
```

## Node.js / NAPI Bridge (`packages/michi-node`)

The Node.js native addon lives in `packages/michi-node` because Cargo requires a separate `cdylib` target definition:

- Public FFI exports, input validation, and bounds checking live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` (numeric newtypes in `napi/num.rs`), compiled only with `michi-core`'s `napi` feature.
- `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` re-exports those functions across the crate boundary via `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`.
- `napi-derive` uses linker sections (`ctor`) to register native functions across crate boundaries without manual wrapper boilerplates.

## NAPI Boundary Contract

The NAPI boundary (`crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`) has a specific constructor discipline that differs from pure-Rust callers:

**NAPI functions always use normalizing constructors (`new()`), never strict ones (`try_new()`).**

- `RetryConfig::new()` normalizes out-of-range inputs silently (clamps `jitter_factor`, floors `max_delay`, etc.). `napi.rs`'s resilience-domain call sites use it this way; making it fallible there would require either `unwrap()`/`expect()` (banned) or a silent fallback to `Default` (defeats validation).
- Pure-Rust callers and tests may use `try_new()` / `validate()` for explicit error signals.
- JS-facing functions report errors via `napi::Error`, not `Result` propagation — validation that can't be normalized (truly invalid JS input) becomes a JS exception at the boundary, not a Rust panic.

This asymmetry is intentional. The NAPI layer operates in a "be maximally resilient to JS input, fail loudly only for truly unrecoverable cases" mode; the Rust library layer operates in a "signal problems explicitly through types" mode.

**Error output path:** When you hold a `DomainError`, call `domain_error.to_call_tool_result()` directly. Do not wrap it in `AgentResponse::as_error()` — that double-wraps the render and loses the typed `error`/`retryable` fields from `structured_content`. Both `AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result()` and `DomainError::to_call_tool_result()` produce structurally compatible `structured_content` JSON (same top-level keys).

---
michi-graph: minor
---

michi-graph: first release. An MIT, dependency-free (`no_std` + `alloc`) crate for deterministic dependency graphs: build with `GraphBuilder`, validate into a `Dag` that reports every problem at once (duplicate nodes, unknown dependencies, self-dependencies, and cycles with members and one shortest loop), then query the topological order, layers, ready sets, ancestors and descendants. Ties break by declaration order or by key, and every output follows the choice. Edge kinds and per-validation edge filters let one graph produce several dags. See `docs/spec/09-graph.md`.

[workspace]
members  = [
  "crates/michi-core",
  "crates/michi-graph",
  "crates/michi-pipeline",
  "packages/michi-node"
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
# No shared `version`: Callisto writes each crate's version itself and keeps michi-core, michi-pipeline and the npm
# package equal through its fixed group (callisto.toml). CI's version-sync job checks they agree.
edition      = "2021"
rust-version = "1.93"
license      = "FSL-1.1-MIT"
repository   = "https://github.com/orin-dx/michi"
authors      = ["Orin DX"]
homepage     = "https://orin-dx.com/tools/michi/"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Exact pin: workspace crates release in lockstep, so a mixed set must never resolve.
michi-core  = { path = "crates/michi-core", version = "=0.4.0" }
# A normal `^` range, not an exact pin: michi-graph versions on its own (MIT consumers outside the michi release
# cycle use it), and no michi-graph type appears in michi-pipeline's public API.
michi-graph = { path = "crates/michi-graph", version = "0.0.0" }
thiserror   = "2"
compact_str = "0.8"
serde       = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json  = { version = "1.0.150", features = ["preserve_order"] }
schemars    = "0.8"
miette      = "7"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["time"] }

[profile.release]
opt-level     = 3
lto           = "thin"
codegen-units = 1

[profile.bench]
inherits = "release"
debug    = true

# Single source of truth for unsafe_code -- every crate in this workspace
# opts in via `[lints]`/`workspace = true`, replacing a hand-copied
# `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` at the top of every lib.rs. Stays "deny" (not
# "forbid") so the napi boundary's local `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` can still
# override it -- see CLAUDE.md's "No unsafe outside napi boundary".
#
# missing_docs / missing_debug_implementations / clippy::unwrap_used /
# clippy::expect_used / clippy::disallowed_types / clippy::must_use_candidate /
# clippy::missing_errors_doc / clippy::missing_panics_doc stay as per-crate
# `#![warn(...)]` inner attributes in each lib.rs instead of living here:
# `[lints]` applies to every target in a package (every integration test,
# bench, and example, not just the lib target), and those lints are
# specifically meant to apply to library code only -- CLAUDE.md's "no unwrap/expect in lib code"
# rule was never meant to cover benches/examples, and doc-coverage doesn't
# make sense for internal test binaries. unsafe_code is the one lint here
# with no such exception (nothing outside the documented napi boundary
# should ever contain unsafe), so it's the only one safe to centralize.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  INSTA_UPDATE: "no"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  # Cheap, standalone check that .prototools is fully proto-installable.
  # This is the ONLY thing in this file that exercises the same
  # moonrepo/setup-toolchain -> proto install path callisto-release.yml's
  # Callisto actions use internally -- without this job, .prototools could
  # break silently and only surface at actual release time (which is what
  # happened: multiple tools here had no working proto plugin, and CI
  # stayed green through all of it since nothing here ever touched proto).
  prototools:
    name: .prototools is installable
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: rustfmt,clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: typos
        uses: crate-ci/typos@bee27e3a4fd1ea2111cf90ab89cd076c870fce14 # v1.48.0

  docs:
    name: Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features
      # Default features on their own: intra-doc links to feature-gated items only break here.
      - run: cargo doc -p michi-core --no-deps

  markdown:
    name: Markdown format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.oxfmtignore --check "**/*.md"

  semver:
    name: SemVer (against crates.io)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-semver-checks
      # The baseline is the latest version of each crate published on crates.io. The release type comes from the
      # pending changesets, translated to cargo-semver-checks' terms: it names release types literally, so a breaking
      # change needs `major` even before 1.0, where Callisto's minor bump (0.3 -> 0.4) is the breaking bump.
      - name: Check API compatibility against the pending release type
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version=$(grep -m1 '^version' crates/michi-core/Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')
          release_type="patch"
          if grep -hqE '^[^:]+:[[:space:]]*major[[:space:]]*$' .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null; then
            release_type="major"
          elif grep -hqE '^[^:]+:[[:space:]]*minor[[:space:]]*$' .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null; then
            if [[ "$version" == 0.* ]]; then release_type="major"; else release_type="minor"; fi
          fi
          echo "Pending release type: $release_type"
          cargo semver-checks check-release -p michi-core -p michi-pipeline --release-type "$release_type"

    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Read rust-version from Cargo.toml
        id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(grep -m1 '^rust-version' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/rust-version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1

This document describes how the `michi` workspace crates fit together.

## Workspace Layout

`michi` is structured as a virtual Cargo workspace (the root `Cargo.toml` has no `[package]`) with two published crates in `crates/` and one unpublished binding crate in `packages/`:

```text
michi (workspace root, virtual manifest)
├── crates/
│   ├── michi-core        # Every sync primitive: toon, kv, hints, recovery, empty, error, status, mcp, audience,
│   │                     #   response (AgentResponse), pipeline (data type), truncate, truncation, resilience, telemetry;
│   │                     #   napi (feature)
│   ├── michi-graph       # MIT, no dependencies: dependency graphs (GraphBuilder, Graph, Dag), validation, order, layers
│   └── michi-pipeline    # Async pipeline execution: Plan, execute/resume, RunRecord, BreakerRegistry, CancellationToken
└── packages/michi-node   # Node.js NAPI cdylib (@orin-dx/michi), publish = false
```

Dependency direction:

```mermaid
graph LR
    core["michi-core"]
    graphcrate["michi-graph (MIT)"]
    pipeline["michi-pipeline"]
    node["packages/michi-node (@orin-dx/michi)"]

    pipeline --> core
    pipeline --> graphcrate
    node -- "features = [napi]" --> core
```

`michi-core`, `michi-pipeline` and `michi-node` version in lockstep (each crate's `version`, kept equal by Callisto), released together as a Callisto fixed group. `michi-graph` is MIT, depends on nothing in michi and versions on its own; `michi-pipeline` takes it through a normal `^` range and keeps its types out of its public API. `michi-pipeline` and `michi-node` depend on `michi-core` through an exact `=x.y.z` workspace pin, so a mixed set never resolves.

## Component Overview

| Crate / Package | Responsibility | Runtime Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `michi-core` | All sync AXI primitives. `toon`: TOON list rendering and parsing with stack-inlined `CompactString` cells. `truncate`: UTF-8 char-boundary content truncation (`floor_char_boundary`). `truncation`: `TruncationOutcome`, the report of what a list cap cut. `resilience`: retry back-off math, `Retry-After` HTTP date parsing, FNV-1a idempotency keys. Response DTOs: `AgentResponse`, `DomainError`, `StatusResponse`, `CallToolResult`, and the `Pipeline` data type. The public `resilience`, `truncate` and `truncation` items are re-exported at the crate root by explicit list. | `thiserror`, `compact_str` (Optional: `serde`, `serde_json`, `schemars`, `miette`, `napi`, `napi-derive`) |
| `michi-pipeline` | Async execution of a validated `Plan` of steps: one `JoinSet` scheduler (sequential or capped parallel), a returned `RunRecord` whose statuses are `michi-core`'s `StepStatus`, `resume` from a record, a keyed `BreakerRegistry`, a per-run `RetryBudget`, `CancellationToken` and a `StepObserver`. Own `ExecutionError` and `PlanError` types, converting into `DomainError` via `From` — not variants of `michi_core::Error`. See `docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md`. | `michi-core`, `michi-graph`, `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `thiserror` (optional: `serde`) |
| `michi-graph` | MIT, `no_std` + `alloc`. Deterministic dependency graphs: `GraphBuilder` declares nodes and kinded edges, `Graph` may hold cycles, and validation returns a `Dag` or every violation at once. Topological order, layers, ready sets, ancestors and descendants, all following one caller-chosen tie-break. See `docs/spec/09-graph.md`. | none |
| `packages/michi-node` | NAPI cdylib shim for `@orin-dx/michi`. Not published to crates.io. | `michi-core` (`napi` feature), `napi`, `napi-derive` |

## Data Composition & Render Flow

`michi` provides two main entry points for formatting output:

1. **`response::AgentResponse` (Fluent Builder)**: Composes TOON lists, KV items, `help[]` hints, and recovery guidance into a unified output buffer. Supports assistant/user audience routing and direct conversion to MCP `CallToolResult`.
2. **Standalone DTOs**: `DomainError`, `StatusResponse`, `AlreadyDone`, and `empty_state()` render themselves directly into agent-readable KV blocks or GitHub Actions annotations without passing through `AgentResponse`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph primitives["Primitives"]
        toon["michi-core::toon"]
        kv["michi-core::kv"]
        hints["michi-core::hints"]
        recovery["michi-core::recovery"]
        truncate["michi-core::truncate"]
        truncation["michi-core::truncation"]
    end

    toon --> AR
    kv --> AR
    hints --> AR
    recovery --> AR
    truncate --> AR
    truncation --> AR

    AR["michi-core::AgentResponse"]

    AR -->|"render() / render_toon() / render_kv()"| text["Plain Text CLI / Tool Stdout"]
    AR -->|"render_for(Audience)"| textaud["Audience-Routed Output"]
    AR -->|"to_call_tool_result()"| mcpresult["mcp::CallToolResult"]
    mcpresult --> mcpjson["MCP Tools/Call JSON"]

    subgraph standalone["Standalone Renderers"]
        err["DomainError"]
        status["StatusResponse"]
        empty["empty_state()"]
    end

    err --> text
    status --> text
    empty --> text
```

## Node.js / NAPI Bridge (`packages/michi-node`)

The Node.js native addon lives in `packages/michi-node` because Cargo requires a separate `cdylib` target definition:

- Public FFI exports, input validation, and bounds checking live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` (numeric newtypes in `napi/num.rs`), compiled only with `michi-core`'s `napi` feature.
- `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` re-exports those functions across the crate boundary via `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`.
- `napi-derive` uses linker sections (`ctor`) to register native functions across crate boundaries without manual wrapper boilerplates.

## NAPI Boundary Contract

The NAPI boundary (`crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`) has a specific constructor discipline that differs from pure-Rust callers:

**NAPI functions always use normalizing constructors (`new()`), never strict ones (`try_new()`).**

- `RetryConfig::new()` normalizes out-of-range inputs silently (clamps `jitter_factor`, floors `max_delay`, etc.). `napi.rs`'s resilience-domain call sites use it this way; making it fallible there would require either `unwrap()`/`expect()` (banned) or a silent fallback to `Default` (defeats validation).
- Pure-Rust callers and tests may use `try_new()` / `validate()` for explicit error signals.
- JS-facing functions report errors via `napi::Error`, not `Result` propagation — validation that can't be normalized (truly invalid JS input) becomes a JS exception at the boundary, not a Rust panic.

This asymmetry is intentional. The NAPI layer operates in a "be maximally resilient to JS input, fail loudly only for truly unrecoverable cases" mode; the Rust library layer operates in a "signal problems explicitly through types" mode.

**Error output path:** When you hold a `DomainError`, call `domain_error.to_call_tool_result()` directly. Do not wrap it in `AgentResponse::as_error()` — that double-wraps the render and loses the typed `error`/`retryable` fields from `structured_content`. Both `AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result()` and `DomainError::to_call_tool_result()` produce structurally compatible `structured_content` JSON (same top-level keys).

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Fail if a permissive crate's shipped dependency tree contains a non-permissive license.
+
+michi-graph is MIT inside an FSL-1.1-MIT workspace: permissive crates depend on it, so nothing FSL (or otherwise
+non-permissive) may enter its normal or build dependencies. Dev-dependencies don't reach consumers and are skipped.
+
+Usage: cargo metadata --format-version 1 | scripts/check-permissive-deps.py michi-graph [more crates...]
+"""
+
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+
+ALLOWED = {
+    "MIT",
+    "Apache-2.0",
+    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
+    "BSD-2-Clause",
+    "BSD-3-Clause",
+    "ISC",
+    "Zlib",
+    "Unicode-3.0",
+    "Unicode-DFS-2016",
+    "CC0-1.0",
+}
+
+
+def permissive(expr: str) -> bool:
+    """An SPDX expression is permissive if some OR-alternative has only allowed AND-terms."""
+    expr = expr.replace("/", " OR ").replace("(", " ").replace(")", " ")
+    for alternative in re.split(r"\s+OR\s+", expr.strip()):
+        terms = [t.strip() for t in re.split(r"\s+AND\s+", alternative) if t.strip()]
+        if terms and all(t in ALLOWED for t in terms):
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    roots = sys.argv[1:]
+    if not roots:
+        print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    meta = json.load(sys.stdin)
+    packages = {p["id"]: p for p in meta["packages"]}
+    nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in meta["resolve"]["nodes"]}
+    failed = False
+    for root in roots:
+        root_ids = [pid for pid, p in packages.items() if p["name"] == root and p["source"] is None]
+        if not root_ids:
+            print(f"error: no workspace crate named {root}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        seen, stack = set(), list(root_ids)
+        while stack:
+            pid = stack.pop()
+            if pid in seen:
+                continue
+            seen.add(pid)
+            for dep in nodes[pid]["deps"]:
+                if any(k["kind"] in (None, "build") for k in dep["dep_kinds"]):
+                    stack.append(dep["pkg"])
+        for pid in sorted(seen):
+            p = packages[pid]
+            license_expr = p.get("license") or ""
+            if not permissive(license_expr):
+                print(f"error: {root} depends on {p['name']} {p['version']} licensed {license_expr or 'unknown'!r}")
+                failed = True
+        if not failed:
+            print(f"{root}: {len(seen) - 1} shipped dependencies, all permissive")
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Fail if a permissive crate's shipped dependency tree contains a non-permissive license.
+
+michi-graph is MIT inside an FSL-1.1-MIT workspace: permissive crates depend on it, so nothing FSL (or otherwise
+non-permissive) may enter its normal or build dependencies. Dev-dependencies don't reach consumers and are skipped.
+
+Usage: cargo metadata --format-version 1 | scripts/check-permissive-deps.py michi-graph [more crates...]
+"""
+
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+
+ALLOWED = {
+    "MIT",
+    "Apache-2.0",
+    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
+    "BSD-2-Clause",
+    "BSD-3-Clause",
+    "ISC",
+    "Zlib",
+    "Unicode-3.0",
+    "Unicode-DFS-2016",
+    "CC0-1.0",
+}
+
+
+def permissive(expr: str) -> bool:
+    """An SPDX expression is permissive if some OR-alternative has only allowed AND-terms."""
+    expr = expr.replace("/", " OR ").replace("(", " ").replace(")", " ")
+    for alternative in re.split(r"\s+OR\s+", expr.strip()):
+        terms = [t.strip() for t in re.split(r"\s+AND\s+", alternative) if t.strip()]
+        if terms and all(t in ALLOWED for t in terms):
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    roots = sys.argv[1:]
+    if not roots:
+        print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    meta = json.load(sys.stdin)
+    packages = {p["id"]: p for p in meta["packages"]}
+    nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in meta["resolve"]["nodes"]}
+    failed = False
+    for root in roots:
+        root_ids = [pid for pid, p in packages.items() if p["name"] == root and p["source"] is None]
+        if not root_ids:
+            print(f"error: no workspace crate named {root}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        seen, stack = set(), list(root_ids)
+        while stack:
+            pid = stack.pop()
+            if pid in seen:
+                continue
+            seen.add(pid)
+            for dep in nodes[pid]["deps"]:
+                if any(k["kind"] in (None, "build") for k in dep["dep_kinds"]):
+                    stack.append(dep["pkg"])
+        for pid in sorted(seen):
+            p = packages[pid]
+            license_expr = p.get("license") or ""
+            if not permissive(license_expr):
+                print(f"error: {root} depends on {p['name']} {p['version']} licensed {license_expr or 'unknown'!r}")
+                failed = True
+        if not failed:
+            print(f"{root}: {len(seen) - 1} shipped dependencies, all permissive")
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:3:`michi-pipeline` runs a static graph of async steps on Tokio and returns a record of what happened to each one. It is an embeddable library, not an orchestrator: there is no server, no persistence, no scheduling across runs and no dynamic dependencies. What it adds over a plain `JoinSet` is the part agents need: an honest status for every step, retries that never blindly replay work that may already have taken effect, and a resume that continues an interrupted run without repeating finished steps.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:43:`StepContext` carries the run id, step id, attempt number (0-based), a cancellation token that is a child of the run's token, and the step's deadline if one is set. `idempotency_key()` is `run_id:step_id`. It stays the same across attempts and across resume, so a step that passes it to a deduplicating downstream gets each effect applied once. The attempt number is for logging and backoff only and is never part of the key.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:60:A step that returns `Cancelled` while the run's token has not fired cancelled itself (its own timer or token, say). Nothing upstream asked it to stop, so it is not a consequence of anything: it ends `Failed`, a root cause whose dependents are skipped with `caused_by` naming it. It never took effect, so resume runs it again like any failed step.

It returns `ResumeError::FingerprintMismatch` if the saved fingerprint is not the plan's and `ResumeError::UnknownStep` for a saved step the plan lacks. When `steps` holds several records for one step, the last one wins, so an append-only log of `StepRecord::in_flight` on start and the finished record on finish rebuilds each step's latest status. A plan step with no saved record is `Pending`.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:106:One scheduler loop drives both modes. It keeps a remaining-prerequisite count per step and a ready set ordered by declaration index, and spawns ready steps onto a `tokio::task::JoinSet` owned by the call, so no step outlives `execute` or `resume`.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:154:`ExecOptions::observer(Arc<dyn StepObserver>)` is called synchronously from the scheduler loop. `on_step_started` fires before a step is spawned and `on_step_finished` fires with each step's terminal `StepRecord`, including skipped steps and, on resume, steps carried over. A closure `Fn(&RunId, &StepRecord)` implements it. Persisting each finished record, plus `StepRecord::in_flight(id, name)` for each started one, lets a caller rebuild the run with `RunRecord::from_parts` after a crash. docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:3:`michi-pipeline` runs a static graph of async steps on Tokio and returns a record of what happened to each one. It is an embeddable library, not an orchestrator: there is no server, no persistence, no scheduling across runs and no dynamic dependencies. What it adds over a plain `JoinSet` is the part agents need: an honest status for every step, retries that never blindly replay work that may already have taken effect, and a resume that continues an interrupted run without repeating finished steps.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:43:`StepContext` carries the run id, step id, attempt number (0-based), a cancellation token that is a child of the run's token, and the step's deadline if one is set. `idempotency_key()` is `run_id:step_id`. It stays the same across attempts and across resume, so a step that passes it to a deduplicating downstream gets each effect applied once. The attempt number is for logging and backoff only and is never part of the key.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:60:A step that returns `Cancelled` while the run's token has not fired cancelled itself (its own timer or token, say). Nothing upstream asked it to stop, so it is not a consequence of anything: it ends `Failed`, a root cause whose dependents are skipped with `caused_by` naming it. It never took effect, so resume runs it again like any failed step.

# 8. Capacity limits

Status: Accepted

## Context

A capacity investigation found inputs that cost far more than their size suggested. Measured on an Apple Silicon laptop, release builds: `ToonOptions::validate` with 50,000 fields took 1.12–1.35 s; a serde `list()` of 10,000 items with one distinct key each allocated 2.84 GiB; the NAPI exports took 3.0–3.4 s and 2.4–2.6 GiB to reject a 100,001 × 100 `rows` array, and 10k × 10 cells sharing one 100 KB JS string grew RSS by 11 GiB. One such call blocks a server thread or Node's event loop.

## Decision

Bound the work every entry point can be asked to do, and reject oversize input before doing it.

- **Core shape caps (michi-core):** `toon::MAX_FIELDS` = 1,000 header fields, `toon::MAX_CELLS` = 1,000,000 cells and `toon::MAX_TRUNCATION_HINT_CHARS` = 256 chars, reported as `ToonError` variants. `list()` checks them right after its key-union pass.
- **NAPI budgets:** exports that take collections or strings take untyped napi values and convert them incrementally (`napi/input.rs`). Lengths are checked first (100,000 rows; 1,000 fields, values per row or items; 10,000 hints or pipeline and partial-success entries). Each call then gets 1,000,000 cells and 64 MiB of string bytes, with 1 MiB per value, hint, reason, message or name, and 4 KiB per identifier. A string's UTF-8 length is charged before it is copied, so a shared JS string cannot amplify.
- **Numbers:** every JS number passes a validating newtype (`napi/num.rs`); none is clamped.
- **Linear algorithms:** duplicate detection uses a set, `resume` indexes the prior record once, and `Plan::new` dedups dependencies in O(1) per edge.

## Alternatives

- No caps, with the cost documented. Rejected: one accidental oversize call (a sparse `list()` input is easy to produce) blocks the host.
- Length checks in the body of typed napi exports. Rejected: napi-derive converts typed parameters in full before the body runs.
- Caps configurable per call. Not built: no consumer needs a larger document for an agent to read, and a fixed cap keeps the contract simple.

## Consequences

| Case                                        | Before                 | After                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `validate`, 50,000 fields                   | 1.12–1.35 s            | rejected in ~1 µs      |
| serde `list()`, 10k × 10k table             | 2.84 GiB               | rejected in ~1.3 ms    |
| NAPI reject 100,001 × 100 rows              | 3.0–3.4 s, 2.4–2.6 GiB | ~0.1 ms, no allocation |
| NAPI 10k × 10 cells sharing a 100 KB string | 1.6 s, +11 GiB RSS     | rejected in ~11 ms     |
| `resume`, 50,000 carried-over steps         | 1.6–2.4 s              | ~21 ms                 |

- Previously accepted oversize input is now an error, so the change shipped in a minor release.
- New exports must follow the same pattern: untyped arguments, lengths first, then the per-call budget.

## Sources

- `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`, "Resolved 2026-10-21 — Capacity limits" (measurements and decisions)
- `docs/spec/02-toon-format.md`, Size limits
- `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md`, Input limits and Numeric boundary
- `crates/michi-core/src/napi/input.rs`, `crates/michi-core/src/napi/num.rs`

# TOON retrieval accuracy

Status: Open

## Question

For list data returned to an assistant, does TOON preserve retrieval accuracy compared with Markdown-KV, and does the result vary by model size?

## Evidence so far

Token counts are measured in [`evals/toon`](../../evals/toon/results.md) (2026-10-21): nine seeded datasets at 5, 25 and 100 rows, rendered by michi-core and compared with pretty and minified JSON, Markdown-KV and a Markdown table under the `cl100k_base` and `o200k_base` tokenizers. For flat lists at 100 rows TOON is a median 47% smaller than pretty JSON, 23% smaller than minified JSON, 33% smaller than Markdown-KV and 7.5% smaller than a Markdown table. On size the Markdown table is the real competitor, so the open question is retrieval accuracy, not tokens.

Retrieval accuracy is still unmeasured. The pilot harness is ready: 94 questions with answers computed from the source data, crossed with the five formats (470 prompts), run by `evals/toon/pilot/run_pilot.py --model-cmd '<command reading a prompt on stdin>'`.

## Method

Use the same list data and retrieval tasks in both formats. Compare answers against a predefined scoring rule across several model sizes. Record model/version, prompt, data, token count, and per-task result so the comparison can be reproduced.

## Decision this blocks

Recommend a default format for assistant-facing list responses, or leave the choice to consumers if results are mixed. Do not claim that lower token count implies better retrieval.

The graph audit found four issues:

1. **Filtered unknown edges still fail validation.** `validate_filtered` applies its predicate only to resolved edges, then reports every unknown dependency. A probe with a filtered-out edge to `missing` returned `UnknownDependency`. This also exposes a model gap: `EdgeRef` cannot represent an edge without a resolved prerequisite. [graph.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/graph.rs:138)

2. **Many separate cycles make reporting quadratic.** Each cycle component triggers allocations sized to the entire graph. A probe of 50,000 nodes in 25,000 two-node cycles took **4.15 seconds** to report. The existing 100,000-node benchmark covers a single cycle, which misses this case. [graph.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/graph.rs:204), [algo.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/algo.rs:146)

3. **A `Decl` from another builder silently attaches an edge to the wrong node** when its numeric index exists in both builders. This can change topology without an error. [builder.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/builder.rs:58)

4. **The shortest cycle path promise fails for a self-loop inside a larger component.** For `a → a`, `a → c`, `c → a`, both `cycles()` and validation return path `[a, c]`, although `[a]` is shorter. Validation still reports the self-dependency. [graph.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/graph.rs:220)

There is also a documentation mismatch: `NodeIx` is called a declaration position, but duplicate declarations are removed before indices are assigned. This affects inspection of an invalid `Graph`; validation prevents that graph from becoming a `Dag`.

`rtk cargo nextest run -p michi-graph --offline` passed all 18 tests. I confirmed the findings with external consumer probes and made no tracked edits.

name: architect
description: Specify a structural correction when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` reveals a recurring defect class, missing domain model, or architectural gap.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Specify a structural correction

## Outcome

Turn a confirmed defect class into a `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable.

## Decision standard

Validate the input against `shared/schemas/finding-report@2.json`, `shared/schemas/implementation-review@2.json`, or `shared/schemas/implementation-result@1.json`. Load `shared/references/architecture/remediation.md`, then the model and language evidence it selects.

Choose the smallest canonical type, domain operation, interface boundary, ownership rule, dependency direction, or invariant that prevents recurrence. Produce one `spec@1` per structural boundary using `shared/schemas/spec@1.json`. Each criterion must be enforceable by compilation, test, lint, or CI and cover required migration or error behavior.

Route completed specs through `scribe:verify-spec`, `scribe:audit-spec`, `scribe:audit-architecture`, and `scribe:gate-spec` in that order. After Navigator and Smith complete the structural change, run `scribe:audit-architecture` in refresh mode.

## Contract

- Input schemas: `shared/schemas/finding-report@2.json`, `shared/schemas/implementation-review@2.json`, and `shared/schemas/implementation-result@1.json`
- Output schema: `shared/schemas/spec@1.json`
- Optional model evidence: `shared/schemas/arch-model@2.json`
- Persistence after a pass: `docs/specs/<id>.json`

## Teams and fallback

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`; use `tracer` for each independent boundary and keep structural remedy selection with the primary `author`.

If a defect crosses independent subsystems, teammates may trace each boundary and its callers. The primary agent must choose one coherent structural remedy and author the spec. For a single boundary, work alone.

## Boundaries

- Do not prescribe a broad rewrite when an enforceable local boundary removes the defect class.
- Do not treat a plausible finding as confirmed without reproducing or reading its evidence.

This is newly found in this audit, not shown to be introduced by the graph commit. Enforce a byte budget for the builder’s retained state and bound direct string exports before NAPI copies where practical.

Live output: `1e-255 → n: 1e-255`, `1e-256 → n: 0`, `1e-300 → n: 0`, `5e-324 → n: 0`. item.aggregated_output:
Every failed attempt is classified by whether it could have taken effect (RFC 9110 §9.2.2). The same class decides whether the executor retries, which terminal status the step ends in, and whether the returned error says replay is safe.

| Class | Errors | Retried | Terminal status if it is the last outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Not executed | `CircuitOpen` or `Cancelled` returned by the step | `CircuitOpen` after its `retry_after`; `Cancelled` no | `NotRun(CircuitOpen)`; for `Cancelled`, `Skipped(Cancelled)` if the run was cancelled, otherwise `Failed` |
| Rejected | HTTP 429 and 503, `Failed { retryable: true }` | yes, every step | `Failed` |
| Ambiguous | timeouts, HTTP 502 and 504, `Interrupted`, `AmbiguousOutcome` | only `Replay::Idempotent` steps | idempotent: `Failed`; otherwise `OutcomeUnknown` |
| Definitive | everything else | no | `Failed` |

Treating 429 and 503 as "not processed" is a convention, not an RFC guarantee, so a step that may have committed its effect must not report them. It reports 502, 504, a timeout or a non-retryable error instead. A step returns `Cancelled` only when it stopped without effect.

A step that returns `Cancelled` while the run's token has not fired cancelled itself (its own timer or token, say). Nothing upstream asked it to stop, so it is not a consequence of anything: it ends `Failed`, a root cause whose dependents are skipped with `caused_by` naming it. It never took effect, so resume runs it again like any failed step.

A server's `retry_after` (on `Http` or `CircuitOpen`, also inside `StepFailed`) is waited in full, even past `RetryConfig::max_delay`: the server said when to come back, and coming back sooner only earns another rejection. `max_delay` caps michi's own exponential backoff (michi-core's `next_retry_delay` keeps that cap; the pipeline applies the server rule on top). The step deadline still bounds the wait: if the wait would end at or past the deadline, the step stops retrying at once and its reason ends `step deadline reached`. Without a deadline, a long hint is waited out, and cancellation interrupts the wait.

A non-idempotent step whose last outcome is ambiguous ends `OutcomeUnknown` and its error is wrapped in `ExecutionError::AmbiguousOutcome`, which is not retryable and converts to a `DomainError` telling the agent to verify whether the operation completed. An idempotent step's ambiguous outcome stays bare and retryable.

## Status model

Payload:
## Pipeline integration review

**No graph migration regression confirmed.** The new `Dag` preserves declaration indices used by the scheduler, and its canonical form preserves the plan fingerprint for valid plans. The pipeline suite passed **118 tests** with all features. An independent probe checked **1,000 generated DAGs** against a separate topological-order implementation and confirmed declaration-independent fingerprints.

### High-priority issue found elsewhere in the pipeline

**Resume can repeat a non-idempotent effect after a non-retryable failure.** A step that commits an effect and returns `ExecutionError::Failed { retryable: false }` ends as `Failed`. [resume](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:338) automatically reruns every `Failed` step, ignoring the error’s replay safety. A temporary consumer probe produced `first_status=Failed, retryable=false, commits_after_resume=2`. The [error contract](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs:35) says `retryable: true` is the step’s assurance that repeating it is safe. This is a **pre-existing semantic defect**, not introduced by `michi-graph`. The terminal model needs to preserve whether an effect may have happened; a generic `Failed` status cannot safely drive resume.

**Crash recovery cannot fail closed when persistence of the in-flight marker fails.** [The scheduler](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/scheduler.rs:164) catches a panic from `on_step_started` and still dispatches the step. If that callback was persisting the in-flight marker, a later crash leaves no saved step record. [Reconstruction](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:273) marks it `Pending`, and resume reruns it. A second probe reproduced two effects after such a missing save. The [spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:154) acknowledges incomplete persistence after observer panics and promises at-least-once execution, so this is a **documented guarantee gap**, not a graph regression. It matters for consumers expecting crash-safe mutation replay: `StepObserver` has no failure result that can stop dispatch.

### Migration-specific concerns

- [Plan construction](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/plan.rs:299) now goes through graph key and edge sorting. The [pipeline spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:167) still describes wide fan-in handling as linear. The repeated-edge lookup no longer dominates, but total graph construction is not linear in general. This is a performance claim to correct and benchmark at realistic plan sizes; I did not measure a production-scale regression.
- [Violation translation](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/plan.rs:374) maps every future `michi_graph::Violation` variant to `TooManySteps`. Because the graph dependency is intended to use a compatible version range, a future variant could become a misleading error. This is a maintainability risk, not a current failing case.
- The structural [fingerprint](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/plan.rs:400) excludes runner behavior, options, and inputs by design. A caller can resume a record against changed effects under the same step IDs and dependencies. The spec assigns that responsibility to callers; the API should avoid presenting the fingerprint as a complete semantic identity.

Reviewed `Plan::new`, validation mapping, fingerprinting, scheduler graph access, execution, records, and resume against the graph and pipeline specs. Temporary probes live under `/private/tmp/michi-pipeline-replay-probe`; no tracked files were edited.

## Review scope and verdict

I reviewed the clean `feat/michi-graph` worktree at commit `83e6025`, including the new crate, its pipeline integration, core and Node boundaries, tests, and release configuration. **I would not publish the current graph API or call the broader v1 replay contract settled yet.** The graph crate has two confirmed correctness defects and a measurable capacity problem. Separately, the pipeline still has a confirmed way to repeat a non-idempotent effect during resume.

The graph migration itself appears sound for valid plans: declaration order and plan fingerprints were preserved in the cases checked. The risks below are specific, reproducible cases, not conclusions drawn from lint patterns.

## Findings to address before release

| Priority | Finding | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **High — graph correctness** | [`validate_filtered`](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/graph.rs:138) filters resolved edges but reports *all* dangling edges. A filtered-out `app → missing` edge still returns `UnknownDependency`. | A caller excluding dev edges, for example, cannot validate a graph containing an unknown dev dependency. The filter’s edge type cannot represent an unresolved target, so this needs an explicit API rule, not just another condition. |
| **High — pipeline replay** | [`resume`](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:338) reruns every `Failed` step. A non-idempotent step can commit, return `Failed { retryable: false }`, and be run again on resume. A consumer probe observed **two commits**. | The error contract says `retryable: true` is the assurance that replay is safe, yet the terminal `Failed` status loses that distinction. This predates the graph change and is a v1 mutation-safety issue. |
| **High — graph capacity** | Cycle reporting allocates graph-sized scratch vectors for **each** cyclic component ([graph.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/graph.rs:204), [algo.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/algo.rs:146)). | Many small cycles make validation quadratic. - **The shortest-cycle promise has a counterexample.** With edges `a → a`, `a → c`, `c → a`, [`cycles()`](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-graph/src/graph.rs:220) reports path `[a, c]` although `[a]` is the shortest closed path through `a`. Validation still reports the self-dependency, so this is a diagnostic defect.

## Architecture and semantic model

The **graph split is coherent in principle**: an MIT leaf crate with no runtime dependencies lets permissively licensed tools use the graph model, while `michi-pipeline` keeps graph types out of its public API. The implementation needs a sharper distinction between *declared edges*, *resolved edges*, and *edges selected for a particular validation*. The full offline workspace run passed **925 tests** with all features. Workspace Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, graph package verification, and the graph license check passed.
